```{r report-setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(ggrepel)
  library(knitr)
  library(patchwork)
  library(readr)
  library(rmarkdown)
  library(scales)
  library(tidyr)
})

ROOT <- normalizePath(getwd(), mustWork = TRUE)
DATA <- file.path(ROOT, "Publication", "datasets")
FIGURES <- file.path(ROOT, "Publication", "figures")
REPORT_SOURCE <- file.path(ROOT, "Publication", "Desmognathus_study_data.Rmd")
AUXILIARY_MANIFEST_PATH <- file.path(
  FIGURES,
  "AUXILIARY_FIGURE_MANIFEST.csv"
)

source(file.path(ROOT, "scripts", "publication", "gbe_theme.R"))
knitr::read_chunk(file.path(ROOT, "scripts", "publication", "build_gbe_figures.R"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

manifest <- read_csv(
  file.path(DATA, "DATASET_MANIFEST.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
auxiliary_manifest <- read_csv(
  AUXILIARY_MANIFEST_PATH,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)

required_auxiliary_columns <- c(
  "auxiliary_id", "title", "basename", "width_mm", "height_mm",
  "final_font_family", "minimum_target_text_pt", "datasets",
  "release_status", "boundary", "legend", "alt_text", "pdf", "png", "tiff"
)
expected_auxiliary_ids <- c(
  "Auxiliary_Wang_style_integrated_te_history_candidate",
  "Auxiliary_Wang_style_diversity_genome_size_candidate",
  "Auxiliary_Path24_development_traits_reference",
  "Auxiliary_Path_DAG_reference",
  "Auxiliary_Wang2025_cross_study_te_diversity_reference"
)
expected_auxiliary_titles <- c(
  "Wang-style integrated TE content and proliferation candidate",
  "Wang-style TE diversity and genome-size candidate",
  "Path24 development and phenotype reference",
  "Path DAG equivalence-class reference",
  "Cross-study TE-diversity reference (Wang et al. 2025)"
)

if (!all(required_auxiliary_columns %in% names(auxiliary_manifest))) {
  stop(
    "Auxiliary figure manifest is missing required columns: ",
    paste(setdiff(required_auxiliary_columns, names(auxiliary_manifest)), collapse = ", ")
  )
}
if (
  !identical(auxiliary_manifest$auxiliary_id, expected_auxiliary_ids) ||
    !identical(auxiliary_manifest$title, expected_auxiliary_titles)
) {
  stop("Auxiliary figure manifest records or order do not match the report contract")
}

manifest_row <- function(supplement_id) {
  row <- manifest %>% filter(.data$supplement_id == .env$supplement_id)
  if (nrow(row) != 1L) stop("Expected one manifest row for ", supplement_id)
  row
}

read_supp <- function(supplement_id) {
  row <- manifest_row(supplement_id)
  read_csv(
    file.path(DATA, row$filename[[1]]),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    progress = FALSE
  )
}

show_table <- function(data, rows = 10L, columns = 12L) {
  rmarkdown::paged_table(
    data,
    options = list(
      rows.print = min(rows, nrow(data)),
      cols.print = min(columns, ncol(data))
    )
  )
}

sha256_file <- function(path) {
  output <- system2("sha256sum", path, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  if (length(output) != 1L) stop("Could not hash ", path)
  strsplit(output, "[[:space:]]+")[[1]][[1]]
}

species_label <- function(x) {
  text <- as.character(x)
  ifelse(grepl("^D\\. ", text), text, paste("D.", text))
}

figure_path <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(FIGURES, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing figure: ", path, ". Run `make figures`.")
  path
}

escape_html <- function(value, attribute = FALSE) {
  htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(value), attribute = attribute)
}

format_inline <- function(value) {
  escaped <- escape_html(value)
  gsub("`([^`]+)`", "<code>\\1</code>", escaped, perl = TRUE)
}

auxiliary_paths <- file.path(FIGURES, auxiliary_manifest$png)
if (any(!file.exists(auxiliary_paths))) {
  stop(
    "Missing auxiliary figure files: ",
    paste(basename(auxiliary_paths[!file.exists(auxiliary_paths)]), collapse = ", "),
    ". Run `make figures`."
  )
}

stopifnot(
  nrow(manifest) == 43L,
  identical(manifest$supplement_id, sprintf("S%02d", seq_len(43))),
  nrow(auxiliary_manifest) == 5L
)
```

<div class="callout">
This is a **read-only researcher-facing view** over the controlled study
release. The CSV files and their hashes remain the data authority. Code chunks
make the filters and equations visible; the report does not overwrite a source
table, review decision, or publication dataset.
</div>

<div class="callout boundary">
**Claim boundaries.** Genome-size values are conditional *D. fuscus*
assembly-anchored pg/1C estimates, not direct independently measured species
C-values. Their assay and conversion evidence is isolated in the calibration
proof below. The anchor is 16.462167689 pg/1C
(`16.1 Gbp / 0.978 Gbp per pg`). The LTR terminal:internal statistic is a
mapping/deletion-footprint proxy, not a direct ectopic-recombination, solo-LTR,
or DNA-loss rate. Cell and nucleus summaries describe the reviewed upper tail
of observed erythrocytes and their intervals are conditional on the observed
animals and images. Current path analyses are exploratory and do not orient a
unique causal arrow.
</div>

# Study report {.tabset .tabset-fade}

## Guide and dataset index

### What is included

- **TE34:** 34 species with accession-linked genomic resources.
- **Path24:** 24 species with finalized conditional genome-size, cell, and
  nucleus data.
- **overlap21:** the exact 21-species intersection; no TE or phenotype values
  are imputed.
- **S01–S43:** controlled CSV supplements with source/output SHA-256 hashes.
- **Figures:** the exact current ggplot figures built by
  [`scripts/publication/build_gbe_figures.R`](../scripts/publication/build_gbe_figures.R).

The report shows compact species-level tables directly. Large object- and
element-level tables remain downloadable CSVs so the HTML stays responsive.

## TE diversity context and Bonsai composition representation

### Diversity equations and primary filter

For proportions \(p_i\) within a species:

\[
H' = -\sum_i p_i \ln(p_i)
\]

\[
D_{GS} = 1 - \sum_i p_i^2
\]

These are natural-log Shannon entropy and the Gini-Simpson index.

Following Wang et al. (2025), the canonical diversity calculation retains each
species's ten most abundant positive TE superfamilies. Those ten proportions
are explicitly reclosed to sum to one before calculating natural-log Shannon
entropy and the Gini-Simpson index. Wang et al. documented the top-ten scope but
did not state whether the retained proportions were reclosed; this report makes
our normalization rule explicit. Unresolved aligned-base mass remains separate
in S07 as dnaPipeTE classification-accounting QC and is not treated as a
diversity category. The 24-shared-superfamily rule below belongs to the Bonsai
composition representation and the retained PCA geometry audit.

```{r diversity-replay}
te_diversity <- read_supp("S08")
superfamily_composition <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data",
    "te_superfamily_composition.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

recomputed_primary <- superfamily_composition %>%
  pivot_longer(-species, names_to = "feature", values_to = "proportion") %>%
  filter(proportion > 0) %>%
  arrange(species, feature) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  slice_max(proportion, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(proportion = proportion / sum(proportion)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_superfamilies_included = n(),
    shannon_entropy = -sum(proportion * log(proportion)),
    gini_simpson = 1 - sum(proportion^2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_primary <- te_diversity %>%
  select(species, n_superfamilies_included, shannon_entropy, gini_simpson) %>%
  arrange(species)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_diversity) == 34L,
  n_distinct(te_diversity$species) == 34L,
  all(te_diversity$n_superfamilies_included == 10L),
  !any(grepl("unresolved", names(te_diversity), ignore.case = TRUE)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_primary, observed_primary, tolerance = 1e-12))
)

te_diversity %>%
  arrange(desc(shannon_entropy)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 4)
```

### Published cross-study top-10 superfamily context

`S41` is a descriptive comparison surface containing 118 records: the exact 84
records deposited for Figure 2 by Wang et al. (2025) and 34 current
*Desmognathus* records. The published numerical data were retrieved from
[Dryad (dataset DOI 10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv)](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv)
under CC0-1.0 and accompany
[article DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3).

Both origins report natural-log Shannon and Gini-Simpson diversity over their
top 10 TE superfamilies, but the pipelines are different and not
method-harmonized. Wang et al. generated the published values from
RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker annotations; the current *Desmognathus* rows use the
same canonical S08 reclosed calculations from retry-averaged dnaPipeTE
compositions. Current
genome sizes are conditional *D. fuscus* assembly-anchored estimates, not
direct species C-values. This is descriptive cross-study context only; no
pooled regression or hypothesis test is performed.

```{r cross-study-diversity-contract}
cross_study_diversity <- read_supp("S41")

origin_counts <- cross_study_diversity %>%
  count(data_origin) %>%
  tibble::deframe()
inclusion_counts <- cross_study_diversity %>%
  count(figure_inclusion) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

stopifnot(
  nrow(cross_study_diversity) == 118L,
  n_distinct(cross_study_diversity$source_record_id) == 118L,
  identical(
    as.integer(origin_counts[c("wang2025_published", "desmognathus_current")]),
    c(84L, 34L)
  ),
  identical(
    as.integer(inclusion_counts[c(
      "published_scatter_and_group", "published_group_only",
      "current_scatter_and_group", "current_group_only"
    )]),
    c(11L, 73L, 21L, 13L)
  ),
  setequal(
    cross_study_diversity$metric_scope,
    c(
      "published_top10_superfamilies_repeatmodeler_repeatmasker",
      "current_top10_superfamilies_dnapipete_retry_averaged"
    )
  )
)

cross_study_diversity %>%
  select(
    data_origin, scientific_name, comparison_group, genome_size_gb,
    shannon_top10_superfamilies, gini_simpson_top10_superfamilies,
    metric_scope, figure_inclusion
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)
```

### Shared CLR composition and retained PCA audit

The Bonsai representation and PCA audit use the same retry-averaged superfamily
compositions: retain features positive in all 34 TE species, close each row,
and apply the centered log-ratio transformation:

\[
\operatorname{clr}(p_{ij}) = \ln(p_{ij}) - \frac{1}{D}\sum_{k=1}^{D}\ln(p_{ik})
\]

For the supplementary PCA audit, columns are centered and an unscaled SVD is
fit. There is no zero replacement in the retained 24-superfamily matrix. CR1,
Chapaev, Dada, Ginger, and Merlin fail the ubiquitous-feature gate. Their
presence does not determine diversity inclusion, which instead uses each
species's abundance-ranked top ten.

```{r pca-contract}
te_scores <- read_supp("S09")
te_variance <- read_supp("S10")
te_loadings <- read_supp("S11")
feature_prevalence <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data",
    "te_feature_prevalence.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

retained_superfamilies <- feature_prevalence %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", pca_included)
excluded_superfamilies <- feature_prevalence %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", !pca_included)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_scores) == 34L,
  nrow(te_variance) == 23L,
  nrow(te_loadings) == 24L,
  nrow(retained_superfamilies) == 24L,
  setequal(
    excluded_superfamilies$feature,
    c("CR1", "Chapaev", "Dada", "Ginger", "Merlin")
  )
)

excluded_superfamilies %>%
  select(
    feature, n_species_positive, prevalence_fraction,
    minimum_proportion, maximum_proportion, pca_exclusion_reason
  )
```

No final sensitivity analysis asks whether forcing CR1 or Chapaev into the
shared-feature representation changes support; the report does not invent one.

### Bonsai publication representation and exact validation

Figure 2 uses the pinned Bonsai fit to the shared 24-superfamily CLR matrix.
S42 binds all 34 tree tips to the expert reproductive-strategy annotation, and
S43 binds the exact fixed-tree permutation and bounded feature-resampling
statistics shown in the figure.

```{r bonsai-contract}
bonsai_tips <- read_supp("S42")
bonsai_validation <- read_supp("S43")

strategy_counts <- bonsai_tips %>%
  count(reproductive_strategy) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

stopifnot(
  nrow(bonsai_tips) == 34L,
  identical(
    as.integer(strategy_counts[c(
      "aquatic_eggs", "direct_development",
      "terrestrial_eggs_aquatic_larvae"
    )]),
    c(7L, 3L, 24L)
  ),
  nrow(bonsai_validation) == 3L,
  all(bonsai_validation$feature_bootstrap_replicates == 200L),
  identical(
    as.integer(bonsai_validation$feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_count),
    c(55L, 70L, 2L)
  ),
  all(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_observed_steps == 2L),
  all(abs(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_null_mean_steps - 9.41320413) < 1e-8),
  all(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_p_value == 0.00001),
  all(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_p_value_holm == 0.00009)
)

bonsai_validation %>%
  select(
    strategy_label, group_n, full_fit_edge_delimited,
    fixed_tree_smallest_side_p_value_holm,
    feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_count,
    feature_bootstrap_replicates,
    feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_fraction
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 3, columns = 7)
```

The rooted Newick is a serialization of a non-phylogenetic TE-composition
representation: branch length is fitted diffusion time and the display root has
no phylogenetic meaning. Strategy labels were supplied after review of the
initial PCA. Localization is therefore post hoc and does not establish causation
or phylogenetically independent association. Feature resampling perturbs the 24
correlated compositional coordinates; it is not a biological-specimen bootstrap.

## LTR terminal:internal depth proxy

### Gate and IQR replay

An eligible element is at least 3,000 bp long, has an exact TEsorter
annotation, is LTR/Gypsy, and has at least five whitespace-delimited
`DOMAIN|MODEL` annotations. The essential filter is inclusive and is computed
within species over the 408 eligible elements:

\[
Q1 - 1.5\,IQR \leq T:I \leq Q3 + 1.5\,IQR
\]

The independent coverage gate requires positive depth across at least 80% of
positions separately in the left LTR, right LTR, and internal region. The
primary branch is the intersection of IQR retention and that coverage gate.

```{r ltr-filter-replay}
ltr_elements <- read_supp("S14")
ltr_species <- read_supp("S15")
ltr_coverage <- read_supp("S16")
ltr_excluded <- read_supp("S17")

count_tesorter_domains <- function(value) {
  text <- trimws(as.character(value))
  if (is.na(value) || text == "" || tolower(text) == "none") return(0L)
  length(strsplit(text, "[[:space:]]+")[[1]])
}

ltr_check <- ltr_elements %>%
  mutate(
    recomputed_domain_count = vapply(Domains, count_tesorter_domains, integer(1)),
    recomputed_domain_gate =
      .data[["element length"]] >= 3000 &
      tesorter_annotation_found &
      Order == "LTR" &
      Superfamily == "Gypsy" &
      recomputed_domain_count >= 5
  )

fences <- ltr_check %>%
  filter(recomputed_domain_gate) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    q1 = quantile(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions, 0.25),
    q3 = quantile(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions, 0.75),
    iqr = q3 - q1,
    lower = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ltr_check <- ltr_check %>%
  left_join(fences, by = "species") %>%
  mutate(
    recomputed_iqr_keep = recomputed_domain_gate &
      ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions >= lower &
      ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions <= upper,
    recomputed_coverage =
      left_ltr_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8 &
      right_ltr_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8 &
      internal_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8,
    recomputed_primary = recomputed_iqr_keep & recomputed_coverage
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(ltr_elements) == 1086L,
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_count == as.integer(ltr_check$domain_count)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate == as.logical(ltr_check$domain_gate_keep)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_iqr_keep == as.logical(ltr_check$iqr_filter_keep)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_coverage == as.logical(ltr_check$coverage_ge_80pct)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_primary == as.logical(ltr_check$primary_ltr_element)),
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate) == 408L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_iqr_keep) == 381L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate & ltr_check$recomputed_coverage) == 407L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_primary) == 380L,
  n_distinct(ltr_check$species[ltr_check$recomputed_primary]) == 30L
)

primary_ltr_species <- ltr_species %>%
  filter(
    analysis_branch == "primary_iqr_filtered_coverage_ge_80pct",
    ratio_median > 0
  ) %>%
  select(
    species, n_elements, ratio_median,
    median_bootstrap_ci_low, median_bootstrap_ci_high,
    fraction_ratio_gt_1,
    median_terminal_positive_coverage_fraction,
    median_internal_positive_coverage_fraction
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ratio_median))

stopifnot(nrow(primary_ltr_species) == 30L)
primary_ltr_species %>% show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)
```

The 1,086-row audit table remains intact; filtering changes branch membership
instead of deleting evidence. No canonical between-species omnibus test has
been finalized for this corrected 380-element branch, so none is added here.


```{r show-figure-4, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 4. LTR terminal:internal mapping/deletion-footprint proxy."}
)
```

## Cell and nucleus morphology

The object table contains 1,152 frozen reviewed cell-nucleus pairs across 24
species; the report does not silently refilter it. Physical area uses the fixed conversion
\(0.0144\;\mu m^2\) per pixel. Species point estimates are medians of the
accepted reviewed pairs.

```{r morphology-replay}
morphology_objects <- read_supp("S18")
morphology_species <- read_supp("S19")
morphology_audit <- read_supp("S20")

recomputed_morphology <- morphology_objects %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_size_cells = n(),
    n_size_images = n_distinct(filename),
    n_size_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    cell_area_um2 = median(cell_area_um2),
    nucleus_area_um2 = median(nuc_area_um2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_morphology <- morphology_species %>%
  select(
    species, n_size_cells, n_size_images, n_size_specimens,
    cell_area_um2, nucleus_area_um2
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

stopifnot(
  nrow(morphology_objects) == 1152L,
  nrow(morphology_species) == 24L,
  all(abs(morphology_objects$cell_area_um2 - morphology_objects$cell_area_px * 0.0144) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(morphology_objects$nuc_area_um2 - morphology_objects$nuc_area_px * 0.0144) < 1e-9),
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_morphology, observed_morphology, tolerance = 1e-9))
)

morphology_species %>%
  arrange(desc(cell_area_um2)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 12)
```

Seven species are represented by one animal. Intervals are conditional
paired-object intervals for the observed reviewed data; they are not
population-level among-animal uncertainty intervals.


```{r show-figure-5, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 5. Phylogenetically aligned conditional genome size and reviewed cellular traits."}
  figure_path("Figure_5_phylogeny_and_cellular_traits.png"),

```

## Conditional genome size

The Path24 analysis and all paper-facing figures use the released
`genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored` field. Values are expressed in pg/1C on a
conditional *D. fuscus* assembly-anchored scale. The intervals propagate the
released measurement bootstrap but not uncertainty in the selected assembly
anchor; these values are not direct independently measured species C-values.

```{r genome-size-table}
genome_size_traits <- read_supp("S04")

stopifnot(
  nrow(genome_size_traits) == 24L,
  n_distinct(genome_size_traits$species) == 24L,
  all(is.finite(genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored)),
  all(genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_ci_low <= genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored),
  all(genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_ci_high >= genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored)
)

genome_size_traits %>%
  select(
    species, genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored,
    genome_size_pg_ci_low, genome_size_pg_ci_high,
    n_genome_size_nuclei, n_genome_size_images, n_genome_size_specimens
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 7)
```

<div class="callout warning">
Figure 6 shows frozen exploratory Pagel-lambda PGLS sensitivities. Its fitted
lines should not be read as causal relationships, and the conditional
genome-size scale should not be mistaken for direct species C-value assays.
</div>

```{r figure-6, eval=FALSE}
```


### Calibration proof: optical density to conditional genome size

Optical density is defined per nuclear-mask pixel from background and observed
intensity; nuclear IOD is the sum of optical density over the mask, not mean
optical density. The species estimator is the arithmetic mean of the
within-image median IOD values. The retained Path24-median relative audit index
is:

\[
IOD_{relative,s} = \frac{\operatorname{mean}_{image}
  (\operatorname{median}_{nucleus}(IOD))_s}
  {\operatorname{median}_{species}(IOD_{equal-image})}
\]

The paper-facing conditional scale instead fixes *D. fuscus* to the selected
rounded pooled assembly span:

\[
G_{reference,1C} = \frac{16.1\ \mathrm{Gbp}}
  {0.978\ \mathrm{Gbp\ pg}^{-1}} = 16.462167689\ \mathrm{pg},
\qquad
G_s = \frac{IOD_{equal-image,s}}{IOD_{equal-image,fuscus}}
  G_{reference,1C}.
\]

Process_413/specimen 32469 and Process_414/specimen 32470 were author-confirmed
as the *D. fuscus* standards and were stained in the same experimental runs as
the unknowns. Their exact standard-to-target run map has not been recovered,
and their median IOD values differ by approximately 41%. This unresolved
calibration/QC evidence is why the resulting pg/1C scale remains conditional.
The relative-IOD fields remain available in S22 for calibration audit, not as
the default paper-facing trait.

```{r iod-calibration-proof}
iod_objects <- read_supp("S21")
iod_species <- read_supp("S22")
iod_images <- read_supp("S23")
iod_balance <- read_supp("S24")
iod_diagnostics <- read_supp("S25")

recomputed_iod <- iod_images %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    iod_equal_image_estimate = mean(image_median_iod),
    n_images = n_distinct(filename),
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
iod_anchor <- median(recomputed_iod$iod_equal_image_estimate)
fuscus_iod <- recomputed_iod %>%
  filter(species == "D. fuscus") %>%
  pull(iod_equal_image_estimate)
genome_size_reference_pg <- unique(iod_species$genome_size_reference_pg)
genome_size_calibration_pg_per_iod <- genome_size_reference_pg / fuscus_iod
recomputed_iod <- recomputed_iod %>%
  mutate(
    relative_iod_index = iod_equal_image_estimate / iod_anchor,
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored =
      iod_equal_image_estimate * genome_size_calibration_pg_per_iod
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_iod <- iod_species %>%
  select(
    species, iod_equal_image_estimate, n_images, n_specimens,
    relative_iod_index, genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

recomputed_balance <- with(
  iod_balance,
  max_abs_standardized_mean_difference <= 0.10 & max_ks_distance <= 0.25
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(iod_objects) == 805L,
  nrow(iod_images) == 51L,
  nrow(iod_species) == 24L,
  length(fuscus_iod) == 1L,
  length(genome_size_reference_pg) == 1L,
  abs(iod_anchor - 950.176112815) < 1e-8,
  abs(genome_size_reference_pg - 16.462167689) < 1e-8,
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_iod, observed_iod, tolerance = 1e-7)),
  identical(
    recomputed_balance,
    as.logical(iod_balance$passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds)
  ),
  sum(!recomputed_balance) == 4L
)

iod_species %>%
  select(
    species, n_nuclei, n_images, n_specimens,
    iod_equal_image_estimate, relative_iod_index,
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored,
    estimate_support, sample_size_support, quality_match_status
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 10)
```

The calibration quality-balance rule is `max |SMD| <= 0.10` and
`max KS <= 0.25`. The four failures remain visible in the released data and by
point shape in Figure 6; they are not silently removed.

```{r iod-quality-table}
iod_balance %>%
  arrange(passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds, desc(max_ks_distance)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 10)
```

## Integrated species views

`S40` is the exact 21-species TE34-by-Path24 overlap. The join is at species
level; genomic and microscopy measurements are not from the same animal.

```{r integrated-data}
te_genome_size_overlap <- read_supp("S40")
organismal_traits <- read_csv(

    ROOT, "analyses", "03_phylogenetic_path", "data",
    "organismal_traits.csv"

stopifnot(

  nrow(organismal_traits) == 37L,
  n_distinct(organismal_traits$species) == 37L
)

te_genome_size_overlap %>%
```

The expert reproductive-strategy categories are retained as vetted organismal
traits, but the interpretation was supplied after review of the initial PCA.
Any overlay is therefore post hoc and descriptive, not a confirmatory test.

## Existing frozen statistical sensitivities

<div class="callout warning">
This tab exposes **existing frozen exploratory outputs** so collaborators can
inspect them. It does not promote them to confirmatory manuscript claims. The
report does not run the previously discussed ad hoc power, omnibus, or
univariate phylogenetic-signal calculations. No final between-species LTR test
or diversity-index group test is added here.
</div>

The Path24 traits are log10-transformed and sample-standardized for the current
three-trait analysis. Pairwise PGLS estimates Pagel's lambda by maximum
likelihood. Genome size is the released conditional *D. fuscus*
assembly-anchored pg/1C trait throughout S04 and S26–S37. The model otherwise
contains nucleus area and cell area only; the possible integrated TE/SVL path
model has not been specified or fitted.

```{r frozen-statistical-tables}
pairwise_pgls <- read_supp("S26")
path_models <- read_supp("S30")
path_stability <- read_supp("S32")
path_simulation <- read_supp("S36")
path_dsep <- read_supp("S37")

pairwise_pgls %>%
  select(
    comparison, spearman_rho, p_value_descriptive_only,
    pearson_r, pearson_p_value_descriptive_only,
    pgls_standardized_beta, pgls_ci_low, pgls_ci_high,
    pgls_p_value, pagel_lambda, n_species
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 3, columns = 11)

path_models %>%
  filter(analysis_type == "primary") %>%
  arrange(delta_CICc) %>%
  show_table(rows = 10, columns = 12)
```

The complete frozen outputs S26–S37 are linked in the Downloads tab. Their
code authority is
[`analyses/03_phylogenetic_path/run_path_analysis.R`](../analyses/03_phylogenetic_path/run_path_analysis.R).

The formal TE-PCA audit remains a supplementary geometry and clustering audit,
separate from the main Bonsai representation and descriptive S08–S11 tables:

```{r te-formal-audit}
te_audit_dir <- file.path(ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data")
te_cluster_diagnostics <- read_csv(

te_trait_tests <- read_csv(

te_phylogenetic_tests <- read_csv(

te_cluster_diagnostics %>%
  select(any_of(c(
    "candidate_id", "representation", "k", "cluster_sizes",
```

No discrete PCA cluster is accepted. The collaborator Path24 species-tree
provenance issue is separate from Bonsai, which is not a species phylogeny. The
PCA audit replay command is `make te-pca`; the Bonsai replay command is
`make te-bonsai`. Neither is rerun while knitting this report.

## Auxiliary review figures

These unnumbered figures are displayed in the exact order declared by
`Publication/figures/AUXILIARY_FIGURE_MANIFEST.csv` and remain outside the
numbered manuscript-figure sequence.

**Wang-style integrated TE-history candidate boundary.** Review candidate, not
a numbered manuscript figure. Six representatives are selected deterministically
from overlap21 conditional genome-size quantiles plus the *D. fuscus* anchor.
Repeat proportions are fractions of aligned RepeatMasker hit bp, not genome
occupancy; divergence bins are not insertion ages.

**Wang-style TE-diversity candidate boundary.** Reproductive-strategy panels
are post-hoc descriptive strata. Conditional genome sizes are assembly-anchored
IOD-derived estimates. The two direct developers are shown without a regression
because n = 2; the other six panels use Pagel-lambda PGLS fits.

**Path24 development and phenotype boundary.** Descriptive review only: the
Path24 tree-aligned view contains 2 direct-development species and 22
aquatic-larval species. D. organi is absent from Path24 because it has no
complete phenotype record. No development mode or phenotype is imputed. The
picogram track contains conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not
direct independently measured species C-values. The supplied tree provenance
remains unresolved.

**Path DAG equivalence-class reference boundary.** The current Path24 analysis
scores 10
testable Markov-equivalence classes, and the auxiliary image shows one
representative DAG for each class. The saturated 6-member class is omitted
because it has no d-separation claim and was not scored. The Genome size node
uses the released conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C estimates, not
direct species C-value measurements. The same genome-size scale is used across
all scored classes. The shown DAGs are representative only and do not orient
unique causal arrows.

**Cross-study TE-diversity reference boundary.** Descriptive cross-study
context only; no pooled regression or hypothesis test. Wang et al. (2025)
values are the published top-10 TE-superfamily indices from Dryad (dataset DOI
10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv; article DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3; CC0-1.0),
generated from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker annotations. Current *Desmognathus*
top-10 indices are reclosed calculations from dnaPipeTE compositions; the
pipelines are different and not method-harmonized. Current genome sizes are
conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not direct species C-values.

```{r auxiliary-review-figures, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
maximum_auxiliary_width_mm <- max(auxiliary_manifest$width_mm)

for (index in seq_len(nrow(auxiliary_manifest))) {
  row <- auxiliary_manifest[index, , drop = FALSE]
  relative_png <- file.path("figures", row$png[[1]])
  width_percent <- 100 * row$width_mm[[1]] / maximum_auxiliary_width_mm

  cat(sprintf(
    '<section class="auxiliary-figure" data-auxiliary-id="%s">\n',
    escape_html(row$auxiliary_id[[1]], attribute = TRUE)
  ))
  cat(sprintf("<h3>%s</h3>\n", escape_html(row$title[[1]])))
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<div class="callout boundary"><strong>Boundary.</strong> ',
      '%s</div>\n'
    ),
    format_inline(row$boundary[[1]])
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<img src="%s" alt="%s" ',
      'style="width: %.3f%%; max-width: 100%%;" />\n'
    ),
    escape_html(relative_png, attribute = TRUE),
    escape_html(row$alt_text[[1]], attribute = TRUE),
    width_percent
  ))
  cat('<div class="auxiliary-copy">\n')
  cat(sprintf(
    '<p><strong>Legend.</strong> %s</p>\n',
    format_inline(row$legend[[1]])
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<p><strong>Release status.</strong> <code>%s</code><br />',
      '<strong>Datasets.</strong> %s</p>\n'
    ),
    escape_html(row$release_status[[1]]),
    escape_html(row$datasets[[1]])
  ))
  cat("</div>\n</section>\n")
}
```
